messages:
sam: quick sync re: policy engine extensibility. we're getting a bunch of special-casing in the resolver for cost-tier heuristics. can we define a plugin boundary?

lee: yeah this is messy. two options: a) keep binary scorer in runtime and add hooks for feature flags, b) move scoring to a sandboxed plugin process (wasm?) with strict API. both have tradeoffs.

nora: ops/security considerations: plugin process increases attack surface but allows per-tenant isolation and easier hot-reload. Wasm runtime gives sandboxing and resource limits.

infra-bot: ci: perf test queued for scoring-proto changes. refer to https://ci.internal/score-proto

tim: pragmatic path: start with a thin plugin API (score(input) -> score + diagnostics) that runs in-process but guarded by a timeout and CPU quota. later migrate to wasm if needed.

sam: agree. define API stable primitive types: route_features (list), tenant_meta (map string->string), candidate_variants (list of ids). output: variant_rank list + short reason_tags. all fields small.

lee: validator implications: plugins must be statically analyzable enough for the compiler to reason about whether a plugin call can change route compatibility (e.g., block vs penalize). define plugin metadata that declares side-effects and required data.

nora: telemetry: for plugin-decisions include plugin_id and brief tag. need opt-out per-tenant. retention same as others.

sam: also want a simulation harness that can stub plugins to replay older scoring logic to compare regressions.

tim: engineer note: ensure plugin API avoids sending full policy blob. send references only (policy_id, version).

lee: action items: 1) sam -> draft plugin API proto + timeout semantics (due Mon) 2) lee -> security review checklist for wasm vs in-process (due Wed) 3) tim -> simulation harness design for plugin stubbing (due Tue) 4) nora -> telemetry opt-out flow + ingestion budget (due Tue).

nora: question: do we want plugin outputs to be considered in the dry-lint/sim stage? probably yes, but with stubs in CI.

sam: yes, dry-lint should run with plugin stubs returning conservative scores. that avoids surprising rollouts.

lee: ok cool. I'll start a repo for plugin stubs and a couple example heuristics. any objections?

nora: none. :thumbsup:

sam: thanks team, will follow up with a short RFC.
